intro: The Oracle at Delphi has stopped answering questions. Instead she has left a set of riddles, each one sworn upon a different god, and the pilgrims take them to their inns and their temples and their workshops and turn them over in the lamplight. The copyists in the town have noticed something strange in their own work: every sheet they finish, however careful they are, carries exactly one slip, and the same slip never repeats. The slips have begun to pile up in a single ledger at the archives, bound and tied, and the keeper of the archives has started calling it the Oracle's errata because no one can say why such tidy errors should fall from the hands of the most careful writers in Greece.
echo: Cut off one head and two grow back.
